members.working:
Identify central metal oxidation states and d-electron count for each complex.

1. [MnCl₄]²⁻: Mn in +2 (Mn²⁺ d⁵). Tetrahedral high-spin paramagnetic, not d²sp³.
2. [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻: Fe in +2 (Fe²⁺ d⁶). Strong-field CN⁻ gives low-spin t₂g⁶ e_g⁰, diamagnetic, octahedral d²sp³ hybridisation.
3. [Co(CN)₆]³⁻: Co in +3 (Co³⁺ d⁶). CN⁻ strong field → low-spin t₂g⁶ e_g⁰, diamagnetic, octahedral d²sp³.
4. [Cu(CN)₄]³⁻: Cu in +2 (Cu²⁺ d⁹) or +1? Typically Cu(I) d¹⁰? But CN⁻ ligand leads to square‑planar/tetrahedral; paramagnetic, not d²sp³.
5. [Co(H₂O)₆]³⁺: Co³⁺ d⁶, H₂O weak field → high‑spin t₂g⁵ e_g¹, paramagnetic, uses sp³d² hybridisation.
6. [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺: Co³⁺ d⁶, NH₃ borderline/strong field → low‑spin t₂g⁶ e_g⁰, diamagnetic, octahedral d²sp³.
7. [NiCl₄]²⁻: Ni in +2 (Ni²⁺ d⁸), tetrahedral or square‑planar; paramagnetic or diamagnetic depending on geometry; not d²sp³.
8. [Co(en)₃]³⁺: Co³⁺ d⁶, en (bidentate) strong field → low‑spin t₂g⁶ e_g⁰, diamagnetic, octahedral d²sp³.
9. [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺: Ti³⁺ d¹, high‑spin paramagnetic, uses sp³d².
10. [PtCl₄]²⁻: Pt²⁺ d⁸, square‑planar dsp² hybridisation, diamagnetic but not d²sp³.

Thus diamagnetic species with octahedral d²sp³ hybridisation are those that are low‑spin d⁶ octahedral complexes: [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻, [Co(CN)₆]³⁻, [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺, [Co(en)₃]³⁺. All four are diamagnetic and have d²sp³ hybridisation.
